alleycvt.name: ALLEYCVT
alleycvt.scope: Documented songwriting workflow; native sound choices are original adaptations.

methods.title: ALLEYCVT — hook/drop dialogue
methods.summary: Let the vocal idea and bass phrase develop together while preserving a clear lead role.
documented_findings: ALLEYCVT describes starting with melody on some songs and the drop on others, then building lyrics around that choice.
steps: Write an original two-bar melody or vocal idea.
Make a bass answer in the spaces between important syllables.
Keep the rhythm identifiable when the vocal is muted; remove competing layers.
Alternate melody-first and drop-first sketches, then keep the stronger hook.

settings.mapping: Use vocal_space_wobble as an original bass starting point.

methods.evidence: Documented artist principle; original implementation exercise
methods.limits: Exact artist settings and a track-specific reconstruction are not established.

methods.title: ALLEYCVT — contrast and revision
methods.summary: Compare a sparse vocal-led sketch and a heavier drop before committing to the arrangement.
documented_findings: The interview describes introducing unfinished IDs in live sets to gauge response.
steps: Export two versions with one deliberate difference: bass density, hook placement or transition length.
Match playback loudness and compare on the same system.
Keep notes about recall and pacing; revise the composition before adding more effects.

settings.original_test: A/B one arrangement change at a time

methods.evidence: Documented artist principle; original implementation exercise
methods.limits: This comparison protocol is an original exercise, not a documented ALLEYCVT measurement workflow.

methods.title: Subtronics — tonal-delay laboratory
methods.summary: Explore pitch from short delay feedback, then reshape the printed mid-bass texture.
documented_findings: Subtronics names tonal delay, saturation, spectral processing and granular audio exploration in a studio interview.
steps: Start with a quiet, short FM sound and keep sub on a separate path.
For an original unsynced tonal-delay experiment, compute milliseconds as 1000 / desired frequency in Hz; confirm the device can reach it.
Start with low feedback and wet level, add restrained saturation and trim the output.
Record manually and edit useful slices; crossfade boundaries and audition pitch.
Compare against the source at equal loudness.

native_options: Delay if its time range permits
settings.not_automatic: No tonal delay or spectral/granular processor is built by the native patch.

methods.title: Subtronics — register and dynamics contrast
methods.summary: Answer a forceful mid-bass gesture with a quieter or differently voiced event.
documented_findings: The MusicTech interview describes alternating loud and quiet events and contrasting parts of the frequency spectrum; it also recounts a minimal square-wave/OTT source for Black Ice.
steps: Write an original call and response on separate phrases.
Make the answer shorter or quieter; move only the texture layer into a contrasting register.
Preserve the sub root instead of transposing the entire low foundation.
For a separate minimal-source study, select a square wave manually and audition multiband compression before adding extra oscillators.

methods.title: Ray Volpe / Volpetron — vocal-hook fakeout
methods.summary: Build anticipation by repeating a small vocal hook before releasing into the bass drop.
documented_findings: Ray Volpe describes chopping a full vocal phrase into a catchy motif and extending the fakeout on SEE YOU DROP.
steps: Record your own or use a properly licensed short vocal phrase.
Slice around clean syllable boundaries; add short fades and retune only when useful.
Repeat a compact original motif through a deliberately extended fakeout.
Remove competing bass hits until the hook has established its rhythm.
Introduce pitch_hook_stab as an original answer; compare timing variations.

settings.manual_stage: Audio slicing, licensing, pitch editing and arrangement are manual.

methods.evidence: Documented artist principle; original implementation exercise
methods.limits: Exact artist settings and a track-specific reconstruction are not established.

methods.title: Ray Volpe / Volpetron — write drop two first
methods.summary: Start with the most intense section, then design a catchier first drop around its core motif.
documented_findings: The SEE YOU DROP interview describes building the second drop first, working backwards toward a catchier first drop, and mixing as production proceeds.
steps: Sketch a strong second-drop idea before building a long intro.
Reduce density for the first drop while retaining a memorable rhythmic identity.
Check kick/sub balance while composing; compare master processing bypassed at equal loudness.
Preserve an unmastered render for later revision instead of copying another producer's gain structure.

settings.levels: No exact Ray Volpe kick, sub or master gain settings were supplied.

methods.limits: Exact artist settings and a track-specific reconstruction are not established.

methods.title: VULPER — dark-space production study
methods.summary: Original darkwave/witch-house exercise pairing a restrained detuned bass with a separate atmospheric layer.
documented_findings: DREAM VAULT carries artist-published dark electro, darkwave and witch house tags.
steps: Use shadow_reese for an original dark bass foundation.
Keep long reverb on a separate filtered pad or texture rather than flooding the sub.
Try a sparse half-time phrase and leave gaps for ambience.
Audition mono and trim long tails where they obscure the next attack.
